## Paragraph 8.1

## Paragraph 9.1

## SECTION 1 – SCOPE OF THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT

## 1.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] In this Practice Direction—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “all proceedings order” means an all proceedings order under section 42(1A) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “CNBC” means the Civil National Business Centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “civil proceedings order” means a civil proceedings order under section 42(1A) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “civil restraint order” means an order specified in CPR Practice Direction 3C paragraph 1(a), 1(b) or 1(c);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “the Damages Claims Portal” (and “the DCP”) means the online portal for managing damages claims managed by HM Courts and Tribunals Service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “DCP email address” means the following email address that is to be used where parties are required by this practice direction to email the court, or where a party is to submit to the court a document that is in electronic format but that cannot be uploaded, or cannot be converted to be uploaded, to the DCP–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] (a) the email address supplied for the CNBC; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] (b) where the parties have received an order from a judge at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, the email address stated for that hearing centre on the “Find a court or tribunal” webpage which can be found at: Find a court or tribunal – GOV.UK (opens in a new tab) .

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “DCP legal representative” means a legal representative who is registered with MyHMCTS and has been granted access to the DCP;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “DCP postal address” means the following address to which any paper documents that cannot be submitted through the DCP or by email may be sent –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] (b) CNBC, St. Katharine’s House, 21-27 St. Katharine’s Street, Northampton NN1 2LH; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] (c) where the parties have received an order from a judge at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, the postal address for that hearing centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “early adopter court” means a County Court hearing centre that has been selected to trial more advanced features within the DCP and is listed on the HMCTS Reform Civil Fact Sheet which can be found at www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmcts-reform-civil-fact-sheets (opens in a new tab) ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “legal adviser” has the meaning given in paragraph 1.2(b) of Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 2E – Jurisdiction of the county court that may be exercised by a legal adviser;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “MyHMCTS” means the online case management tool managed by HM Courts and Tribunals Service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1] “notification longstop date” means 12 midnight at the end of the calendar day four months after the date of issue of the claim

## 1.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2] (1) This Practice Direction—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2] (a) establishes a pilot to test an online claims process called “Damages Claims”. Damages Claims are managed using the Damages Claims Portal (“DCP”); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2] (b) sets out the circumstances in which the DCP must be used.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2] (2) The pilot applies in the County Court.

## 1.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.3] The pilot will run from 28 May 2021 until 1 October 2026.

## 1.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.4] This Practice Direction sets out the procedure to be followed when using the DCP. The Civil Procedure Rules (“CPR”) will apply to Damages Claims save that where provisions in this Practice Direction conflict with other provisions in the CPR or other practice directions (“PD”), this Practice Direction takes precedence until the claim is transferred out of the DCP. Once the claim is transferred out of the DCP, this Practice Direction will no longer apply. The transfer of a claim out of the DCP does not affect the validity of any step taken prior to transfer.

## 1.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.5] (1) The following are available from links on the DCP—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.5] (a)   guidance on the operation of the DCP;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.5] (b)   a “dummy version” of the DCP with copies of the DCP screens that need to be completed to start a claim or to respond to a claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.5] (c)   specification documentation for the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.5] (2) The documents identified in sub-paragraph (1) are not part of this Practice Direction.

## 1.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (1) The conditions for using the pilot are set out in sub-paragraph (3).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (2) If all of the conditions in sub-paragraph (3) are met—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (a) the claimant’s legal representative must register with MyHMCTS and secure access to the DCP before the claim is started;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (b) the claimant must give the defendant the notice referred to in paragraph 1.9(2)(a) unless it is impractical to do so; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (c) the claim must be started using the procedure set out in this Practice Direction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (3) The conditions referred to in sub-paragraph (1) are—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (a)   the claim is a claim for damages only;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (b)   the claim would not ordinarily follow the Part 8 procedure;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (ba) the claim is not one that could be started online using the Production Centre under Practice Direction 7B Production Centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (bb) the claim is not one that could be started online using Money Claim Online under Practice Direction 7C – Money Claim Online;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (c)   the claim is not made under one of the provisions of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 specified in CPR PD 49C paragraph 3.1;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (d)  the claimant is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (e)  if an individual, the claimant is aged 18 years or over, or is under 18 and has a litigation friend (in which case a statement of suitability must be provided);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (f)     the claimant is not a protected party within the meaning of CPR 21.1(2)(d);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (g)   the fee for issuing the claim is paid in full using any method permitted by HMCTS;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (ga) the claimant will not, before submitting their claim, apply for remission or part remission of a fee prescribed by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (h)   the claim is conducted in English;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (i)     the claimant does not have in force against them—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (i)       a civil proceedings order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (ii)      an all proceedings order; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (iii)    a civil restraint order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (j)     the claimant believes that the defendant—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (i)     has a postal address for service within England and Wales;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (ii)  if an individual, is aged 18 years or older; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (iii)  is not a protected party; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (iv) is not the Crown;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (k) the claim is not one to which Practice Direction 27B applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (l) the claim—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (i) is brought by one claimant against either one or two defendants; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.6] (ii)  is brought by two claimants against one defendant.

## 1.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.7] The notification longstop date applies whether or not it falls on a weekend or public holiday (which means Christmas Day, Good Friday or a Bank Holiday). In respect of every other time limit provided by this Practice Direction—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.7] (a) if it would otherwise fall at 4pm on a weekend or public holiday, the time limit is automatically extended to 4pm on the next business day; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.7] (b) if it would otherwise fall at midnight at the end of a day which is a weekend or public holiday, the time limit is automatically extended to midnight at the end of the next business day.

## 1.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8] Where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8] (a) a party is required to verify a document by signing a statement of truth; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8] (b) that document (or the content of that document) is to be uploaded to the DCP; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8] (c) a party otherwise provides information to the court using the DCP,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8] the requirement for a signature is satisfied by the person who is verifying the document typing their name beneath the statement of truth or clicking a checkbox confirming the statement of truth.

## 1.8A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8A] (1)      Where a document is uploaded to the DCP it is for all purposes filed with the court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8A] (2)      If a document is to be served and can be uploaded to the DCP, the document may only be served by uploading it to the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.8A] (3) Service is deemed to have taken place at the time and date at which the notification is sent by the DCP to the party being served that the document has been uploaded to the DCP.

## 1.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (1)  If all of the conditions in sub-paragraph (2) are met—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (a)  the defendant’s legal representative must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (i) register with MyHMCTS and secure access to the DCP before the claim is started;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (ii)  notify the claimant that they are instructed; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (iii) provide the claimant with their email address for claim notifications; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (b)  the claimant must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (i) provide the defendant’s legal representative’s email address for claim notifications to the court using the DCP when starting the claim under section 2 of this Practice Direction; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (ii) notify the claim to the defendant using the procedure set out in section 3 of this Practice Direction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (2)  The conditions referred to in sub-paragraph (1) are—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (a)  the claimant gives the defendant at least 14 days’ notice of their intention to bring a claim using the DCP; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 1.9] (b)  the defendant has instructed a legal representative before the claim is started.

## SECTION 2 – STARTING A CLAIM

## 2.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (1) To request the issue of a claim form the claimant must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (a)   complete the claim form using the DCP’s screens;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (b) submit the claim form using the DCP, by selecting the “submit” button; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (c)  pay, through the DCP, the appropriate fee that is prescribed in the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008.”.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (2) By selecting the “submit” button the user thereby—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (a)   verifies the brief details of claim by a statement of truth for the purposes of CPR Part 22 and CPR 32.14; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (b)   requests that the court issues a claim form.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1] (3) Unless the document cannot be uploaded to the DCP, any document which the claimant wishes to file or is required to file with the claim form must be uploaded to the DCP, and must be in one of the machine-readable formats accepted by the DCP.

## 2.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (1) The court must notify the claimant by e-mail when the claim is received by the court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (2) Notification of receipt does not constitute notice that the claim form has been issued.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (3) The court must issue the claim form when payment of the appropriate fee is confirmed.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (4) The claim is brought for the purpose of the Limitation Act 1980 and any other period of limitation at the point at which the claim is issued, and not before. CPR PD 7A paragraph 6.1 does not apply.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (5) The court must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (a)   notify the claimant by e-mail when the claim is issued and of the date of issue; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 2.2] (b)   provide the issued claim form to the claimant via the DCP.

## SECTION 3 – NOTIFYING CLAIM AND CLAIM DETAILS TO DEFENDANT

## 3.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.1] The claimant must notify the claim to the defendant. After notifying the claim to the defendant the claimant must notify the claim details to the defendant.

## Sub-section A. Defendant represented by a DCP legal representative at the time the claim starts

## 3.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.2] This Sub-section A applies if the claimant, when starting the claim, provided the court, through the DCP, with the name of the DCP legal representative for the defendant.

## 3.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] (1)  The claimant must notify the defendant of the claim through the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] (2)  Notification of the claim constitutes service of the claim form in accordance with CPR 7.5(1).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] (3)  When the defendant is notified of the claim—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] (a) all parties must be notified of the date of notification;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.3] (b) the defendant must be notified of the date of issue of the claim, through the DCP.

## 3.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.4] The claimant must comply with paragraph 3.3(1) before the notification longstop date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.4] Examples:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.4] Claim form issued on 31 May 2021. The claimant must notify the defendant of the claim before midnight at end of 30 September 2021.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.4] Claim form issued on 9 June 2021. The claimant must notify the defendant of the claim before midnight at end of (Saturday) 9 October 2021.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.4] Claim form issued on 28 February 2022. The claimant must notify the defendant of the claim before midnight at end of 28 June 2022.

## 3.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.5] Notification of the claim, or any documents provided, may be amended or added to, using the DCP, at any time before they have been notified to the defendant.

## 3.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.6] (1) The claimant must provide the details of the claim (the Particulars of Claim and any supporting documents) through the DCP, by completing the relevant screens.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.6] (2) Unless the document cannot be uploaded to the DCP, any document which the claimant wishes to file or is required to file in support of their claim must be uploaded to the DCP, and must be in one of the formats accepted by the DCP.

## 3.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.7] The details must include the information required by CPR 16.4.

## 3.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.8] The details of the claim or any documents provided may be amended or added to, using the DCP, at any time before they have been notified to the defendant.

## 3.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.9] (1) The claimant must notify the defendant of the details of the claim by 4pm on the 14th day after that defendant was notified of the claim, subject to sub-paragraph (1A).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.9] (1A) The claimant must notify the details of claim to the defendant no later than the notification longstop date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.9] (2)  All parties must be notified of the date of notification through the DCP.

## Sub-section B. Defendant not represented by a DCP legal representative at the time the claim starts

## 3.10

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.10] This Sub-section B applies if the claimant, when starting the claim, notified the court, through the DCP, that the defendant was not represented by a DCP legal representative.

## 3.11

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (1) The claimant must comply with Sub-section A above, subject to the modifications in sub-paragraphs (1A) and 1(B).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (1A) A claimant complies with paragraph 3.3(1) (notification of claim) by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (a) serving the claim form that is generated by the DCP in accordance with CPR rule 7.5(1); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (b) notifying the court of service of the claim form before the earlier of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (i) 4pm on the 14 th day after compliance with paragraph (a); and;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (ii) the notification longstop date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (1B) A claimant complies with paragraph 3.6(1) (notification of details of claim) by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (a) serving the details of the claim in accordance with CPR rule 6.20; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (b) notifying the court of service of details of the claim before the earlier of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (i) 4pm on the 14 th day after compliance with paragraph (a); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (ii) the notification longstop date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (2) If, within 14 days of compliance with paragraph (1B)(a), the court receives any paper notification from the defendant, the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (3) Unless, within 14 days of compliance with paragraph (1B)(a) –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (a) the defendant gives notice that they are represented in accordance with Sub-section E below (in which case the court must notify the claimant); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.11] (b) the court has already transferred the claim out of the DCP, paragraph 6.6 does not apply and the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP at the end of the 14 days to the CNBC to continue as if it had started under CPR Part 7, including as to any request or application for judgment in default.

## 3.12

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] If there are two defendants, and one defendant is not represented by a DCP legal representative at the time the claim starts –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] (a) in relation to the defendant that is represented by a DCP legal representative at the time the claim starts, Sub-section A applies, except that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] (i)  the claimant must serve a paper version of the claim form, and must also use the DCP to notify that defendant of the claim within 14 days of the date of service of the claim form;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] (ii) paragraph 1.8A is disapplied; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] (iii) the response time is to be calculated by reference to the date of service of the details of claim stated on the notification of service on the other defendant, and paragraph 6.3 is modified accordingly; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.12] (b) in relation to the defendant that is not represented by a DCP legal representative at the time the claim starts, Sub-section B applies.

## Sub-section D. Notification of service

## 3.13

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.13] (1) Subject to subparagraph (3) below, a party notifies the court of service by completing the relevant screens on the DCP to notify service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.13] (2) Where a party notifies the court of service, the court must notify all parties.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.13] (3) Where the party is required to notify the court of service of a document on more than one party, and where service took place on different days, a party notifies the court of service by filing paper certificates of service at the CNBC.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.13] (4) If the court receives paper certificates of service in accordance with paragraph (3) above, the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC.

## Sub-section E. Notice of representation

## 3.14

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.14] A party gives notice of change of representation under this Sub-section E by using MyHMCTS to file notice of change of solicitor in circumstances where the person named in the notice of change as taking over representation is registered with MyHMCTS and has been provided with access to the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.14] (Paragraph 8.7 sets out how else notice of change of representation can be given.)

## Sub-section F Extension to Notification Longstop Date

## 3.15

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 3.15] If an order is made before the notification longstop date extending the time for notification of the claim or details of claim then the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC to continue as if it had started under CPR Part 7.

## SECTION 4 – FAILURE TO NOTIFY THE CLAIM OR DETAILS OF CLAIM

## 4.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.1] (1) Subject to sub-paragraph (2), if the claimant has not before the notification longstop date notified the defendant of the claim and where sub-section 3B applies complied with paragraph 3.11(1A)(b), then the claim against the defendant will be automatically dismissed without the need for any further order.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.1] (2) If, before the notification longstop date, the claimant notifies the court by email that the parties have agreed an extension of time for notification of the claim, the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC.

## 4.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.2] If the claim is dismissed under paragraph 4.1, it will cease to be governed by this practice direction. Any further action by the parties in relation to the claim would need to be made in accordance with the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules. For example, any application to reinstate a claim that has been dismissed under paragraph 4.1(1) will have to be made by an application on paper under Civil Procedure Rules Part 23.

## 4.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3] (1) Subject to sub-paragraph (2), if the claimant has not by the time calculated in accordance with paragraph 3.9 notified the defendant of the details of the claim and where sub-section 3B applies complied with paragraph 3.11(1B)(b), the claim against the defendant will be automatically dismissed.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3] (2) If, before the time calculated in accordance with paragraph 3.9, the claimant notifies the court by email that the parties have agreed an extension of time for notification of details of the claim, the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC.

## 4.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 4.4] If the claim is dismissed under paragraph 4.3, it will cease to be governed by this practice direction. Any further action by the parties in relation to the claim would need to be made in accordance with the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules. For example, any application to reinstate a claim that has been dismissed under paragraph 4.3(1) must be made by an application on paper under Civil Procedure Rules Part 23

## SECTION 5 – DEFENDANT’S ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF CLAIM

## 5.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (1) The defendant may acknowledge the claim after notification of the details of the claim.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (2) An acknowledgement under sub-paragraph (1) must be given through the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (3) Subject to paragraphs (1) and (2), the defendant must acknowledge the claim if they wish to challenge the court’s jurisdiction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (4) Where the defendant acknowledges the claim under paragraph (3) the defendant must, within 14 days after acknowledging the claim make an application to challenge the court’s jurisdiction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (Section 7A contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (5) Where the defendant makes an application to challenge the court’s jurisdiction the claim must be transferred out of the DCP to continue in the CNBC as if it had been started under CPR Part 7.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1] (6) If the claim is transferred out of the DCP under sub-paragraph (5), paragraph 8.4 will apply.

## 5.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 5.2] The time within which the defendant may acknowledge the claim expires at 4pm on the 14th day after notification of the details of the claim.

## SECTION 6 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO CLAIM

## 6.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1] The defendant must respond to the claim by the time stated on the DCP.

## 6.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2] (1) The parties may agree an extension of time without making an application, provided that only one extension may be agreed and that extension is of 28 days. The defendant must record on the DCP any such agreed extension of time before the expiry of the time limit stated on the DCP. The time limit will then be amended on the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2] (Section 7A makes provision for making applications.)

## 6.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3] The time stated on the DCP for the purposes of paragraph 6.1 is—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3] (a)   4pm on the 14th day after the claimant notified the defendant of the details of the claim (if the defendant has not acknowledged the claim under section 5 and no alternative date has been set);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3] (b)   4pm on the 28th day after the claimant notified the defendant of the details of the claim (if the defendant has acknowledged the claim under section 5 and no alternative date has been set); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3] (c)   such other date stated on the DCP following the agreement of the parties under paragraph 6.2(1) or following an order of court.

## 6.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.4] (1) The defendant must respond to the claim through the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.4] (2) If the defendant indicates that they—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.4] (a)   admit all or part of the claim; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.4] (b)   wish to make a counterclaim,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.4] the claim will be automatically transferred out of the DCP to continue in the CNBC and paragraph 8.4 will apply.

## 6.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (1) If the defendant indicates that they will defend all of the claim, they must submit—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (a)   the details of their defence; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (b)   the directions questionnaire, including if the claim appears suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track,  proposed directions,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] by completing the relevant screens, and selecting the “submit response” button, on the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (2) The defendant’s response must include the information required by CPR 16.5.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (3) Unless the document cannot be uploaded to the DCP, any document which the defendant wishes to file or is required to file with their defence must be uploaded to the DCP, and must be in one of the machine-readable formats accepted by the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (4)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (a)   the claimant must be notified when the defendant has submitted details of their defence; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (b)   all parties must be notified of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (i)       the date of notification; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.5] (ii)      the date by which the claimant must provide initial case management information.

## 6.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (1) Unless sub-paragraph (4) applies, if the defendant does not respond to the claim by the time specified in paragraph 6.3, the claimant may ask for judgment in default of a response to the claim by requesting judgment through the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (2) A claimant requests judgment through the DCP by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (a) completing the relevant screens on the DCP; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (b) submitting the completed screens using the DCP.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (3)  Judgment is to be entered following a request made under sub-paragraph (2) if at the date of making the request –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (a)   the defendant has not responded to the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (b) the defendant has not applied to strike out the claim, or, if the defendant has applied to strike out the claim, that application has been disposed of;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (c)   no party has applied for summary judgment under CPR Part 24, or, if any party has applied for summary judgment under Part 24, that application has been disposed of; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (d)  the defendant has not satisfied the whole claim, including costs.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (4) If the defendant does not respond to the claim by the time specified in paragraph 6.3 and –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (a) CPR rule 12.11 would apply if the claim had been started under CPR  Part 7; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (b) there is a moratorium in place under the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space Moratorium and Mental Health Crisis Moratorium) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] the claimant may not request judgment in default through the DCP but may instead make an application for default judgment.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.6] (Section 7A contains provisions about applications.)

## 6.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] (1) If—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] (a)   the defendant fails to respond to the claim by midnight on the date 6 months after the date of notification of the details of the claim or by that time as extended by any order following an application made before the expiry of the original 6 month period;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] (b)   the claimant has not made a request or applied for judgment under paragraph 6.6; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] (c)   the claimant has not made an application under paragraph 8.1,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] the claim will be automatically dismissed.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 6.7] (2) If the claim is dismissed under sub-paragraph (1), it will cease to be governed by this practice direction. Any further action by the parties in relation to the claim would need to be made in accordance with the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules.

## SECTION 6A – INFORMING THE COURT THAT THE CLAIM HAS BEEN SETTLED AND DISCONTINUANCE

## Informing the court that the claim has been settled

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Informing the court that the claim has been settled] 6A.1-(1) If the claim has been settled then, subject to sub-paragraph 6A.1(5) below, the claimant must use the DCP to tell the court that the claim has been settled, whereupon the proceedings must be stayed. The court must notify the defendant and tell them they may contact the court, on time, to object.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Informing the court that the claim has been settled] (2) The defendant contacts the court on time if they contact the court within 19 days after notification by the court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Informing the court that the claim has been settled] (3) If the defendant objects on time, the court must transfer the claim out of the DCP to the CNBC or where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to that hearing centre.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Informing the court that the claim has been settled] (4) A claimant must only notify the court of settlement under this Section if all matters in dispute are settled including who must pay the court fee and who must pay the costs of the proceedings. If there remains a dispute over the amount of costs then an application for an order can be made following the settlement to lift the stay and for the court to make an order to give effect to the settlement so far as it relates to costs.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Informing the court that the claim has been settled] (5) If a party requires the terms of settlement to be incorporated into an order then (notwithstanding any notification in accordance with sub-paragraph 6A.1 (1) above)  the claimant must make an application including the agreed form of order.

## Discontinuance

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] 6A.2-(1) In a claim not falling within subparagraph (3), if a claimant wishes to discontinue all or part of their claim, the claimant complies with CPR 38.3(1)(a) by filing the notice of discontinuance required by that rule—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) at the CNBC; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, that hearing centre.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (2) If the claimant files a notice of discontinuance pursuant to subparagraph (1), the claim must be transferred out of the DCP to continue in the CNBC, or where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to continue in that hearing centre as if it had been started under CPR Part 7.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (3) A claim falls within this subparagraph if—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) there are two parties; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) there are more than two parties, and—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (i) where there are two claimants, each wishes to discontinue their claim against the defendant to the same extent as the other; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (ii) where there is one claimant, they wish to discontinue their claim against both defendants to the same extent.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (4) Where the claim falls within subparagraph (3)—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) the claimant (or each claimant, if there are two) must  discontinue all or part of their claim by completing the relevant  screens on the DCP in order to comply with CPR 38.3(1)(a) and (b), (2), (3) and (5);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) the effective date for the purposes of CPR 38.5(1) is the date the notification is sent via the DCP to the defendant (or  defendants, if there are two) in accordance with paragraph  1.8A(3) that the claimant has (or claimants have, if there are two) completed the relevant screens in accordance with  paragraph (a) above.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (5) If the claimant (or both claimants) discontinue all or part of their claim pursuant to subparagraph (4)(a), the claim will continue to remain within the DCP until a step can no longer be supported at which point it  will be transferred out of the DCP to continue in the CNBC, or where  the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a  County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to continue in that  hearing centre as if it had been started under CPR Part 7.

## SECTION 7 – INITIAL CASE MANAGEMENT

## 7.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.1] (1) If the defendant responds to the claim with a defence, the claimant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.1] (a)  indicate whether they want to continue with the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.1] (b) if they do want to continue with the claim, provide hearing information using the DCP, including if the claim appears  suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, proposed  directions,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.1] before 4pm on the 28th day after date of notification of the defendant’s response.

## 7.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.2] CPR 26.6 does not apply to claims started using the DCP.

## 7.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.3] Omitted

## 7.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.4] If the claimant does not comply with paragraph 7.1 within the time specified in that paragraph—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.4] (a)   the claim will, at that point, be transferred out of the DCP to a County Court Hearing Centre pursuant to paragraph 8.1;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.4] (b)   the claim will be treated in the same way as if the claimant had failed to comply with a notice served under CPR 26.4(1); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.4] (c)   an order will be made under CPR 26.4(9).

## 7.4A Omitted

## 7.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.5] In those claims to which the provisions of Section II of CPR Part 3 and Practice Direction 3D apply, CPR 3.13(1)(a) is disapplied and all parties except litigants in person must file and exchange budgets in accordance with CPR 3.13(1)(b), namely not later than 21 days before the first case management conference.

## 7.6

## Claims allocated to the fast track –Trial readiness certificate

## 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (2) CPR Rule 28.4 and 28.5 do not apply, except to the extent provided for by subparagraph (6).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (3) Within 2 weeks of notice from the court via the DCP to do so, the parties must use the relevant screens on the DCP to complete and submit a “trial readiness certificate”, to indicate whether they are ready for trial and to update any hearing requirements already given to the court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (4 ) As soon as practicable after the date that all trial readiness certificates are submitted, the court shall—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (a) fix the date for the trial, unless it has already done so;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (b) give any directions for the trial, including a trial timetable, which it considers appropriate; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (c) specify any further steps that need to be taken before trial,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] and the court shall give the parties at least 3 weeks’ notice of the date of the trial unless, in exceptional circumstances, the court directs that shorter notice be given.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (5)  Notwithstanding that the parties must complete a trial readiness certificate, a judge may nevertheless direct that a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) be sent to the parties for completion as well.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (6) If a pre-trial checklist is sent to the parties for completion under subparagraph (5)–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (a) CPR rule 28.4 applies with the following modification: rule 28.4(1) applies as if it permits (but does not require) the court to send the parties a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) for completion and return in accordance with that rule;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (b) CPR PD 28 paragraph 6.1(2) similarly applies as if it permits (but does not require) the court to send out Forms N170 and N171 to the parties; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6(1) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (c) CPR rule 28.5 applies.

## Claims allocated to the intermediate track or the multi-track – pre-trial checklists

## 7.6A This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to intermediate track or the multi-track.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 7.6A This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to intermediate track or the multi-track.] (2) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4, 28.5, 29.6 and 29.7 do not apply, except to the extent provided for by subparagraph (4) and (5).

## 12

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (3) A judge may direct that parties must complete and upload to the DCP a pre- trial checklist (listing questionnaire) – Form N170).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (4) If the claim is allocated to the intermediate track and a judge directs that the parties complete and upload a pre-trial checklist under subparagraph (3)–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (a) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4 applies with the following modification –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (i) rule 28.4 applies as if a reference to filing or returning includes filing or returning by uploading to the DCP;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (ii) rule 28.4(1) applies as if it permits (but does not require) a judge to direct that parties must complete and upload a pre-trial checklist (listing questionnaire) in accordance with that rule;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZB – THE DAMAGES CLAIMS PILOT > 12] (iii) rule 28.4(3) applies as if, if no party uploads a pre-trial checklist by the date specified in the notice of allocation, the claim is to be referred to a judge for directions; and
